title: The Shabbat of return (Hosea 14:2)
hook: the Shabbat between, with Hosea's "Return, O Israel"

segments.voice: Yesterday, teshuvah and the ten days of return. Your line was ten days to turn. Today, the one Shabbat inside those ten days, and the end of a week.

Every year, between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, there's exactly one Shabbat. It has its own name, taken from the first word of its prophetic reading. In many communities the rabbi gives a long sermon that day, all about coming back. Otherwise it looks like any other Shabbat: candles, a long meal, an afternoon nap. And the reading opens with a single Hebrew word, shuvah. Return.
screen: `ONE SHABBAT BETWEEN.` → `A SERMON ABOUT COMING BACK.` → `SHUVAH: RETURN.`

segments.voice: Shabbat Shuvah is named for the haftarah from the prophet Hosea: "Return, O Israel, unto the LORD thy God; for thou hast stumbled in thine iniquity." Notice the word Hosea chooses. Not you have rebelled, not you are wicked. Stumbled. You tripped; you can get up. The next verse gives instructions, and they're surprising: "Take with you words, and return unto the LORD." Not sacrifices, not gold, not a grand gesture. Words. Hosea goes on: instead of bulls, we'll offer the words of our lips. Later rabbis leaned on this verse when the Temple was gone: prayer could stand in for the offerings. The reading ends in tenderness. God promises to heal, to love freely, to be like dew to Israel, so that it blossoms like a lily. Some call this day Shabbat Teshuvah, the Shabbat of repentance. Shuvah is the command form: come back. Much of the Days of Awe speaks the language of a court: judgment, books, seals. Shabbat Shuvah sounds more like a parent standing at the door. You stumbled. Come back. Bring words. On the day of rest itself, the whole season comes down to its simplest version: return.
screen: `SHUVAH: COME BACK.` · `YOU STUMBLED; YOU CAN GET UP.` · `TAKE WITH YOU WORDS.` · `LIKE DEW, LIKE A LILY.` · then, large: `RETURN.`

segments.voice: Think of one place where you stumbled this year, just one, and take Hosea's advice: find the words you'd say if you were coming back, and say them quietly in your own language, to God if you pray, or to yourself as someone who can get up. Then breathe, and picture dew on grass in the morning.
Shabbat Shuvah. The Shabbat of return, between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, named for Hosea's call: return, O Israel.
Your line: return. A week of who is king, a sigh and a sob, Hannah heard, the boy heard, write us in, ten days to turn. Day six hundred fifty-one, done.

howItsDone: On the Shabbat between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, the haftarah from Hosea 14 (with additions from Joel or Micah, by custom) is read, and many rabbis give a major sermon on teshuvah.
